title: Sales and Advisor Analysis reports drop a voided invoice and keep its re-invoice
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission and can create and invoice work orders.
  • Location {Location-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Quiet 14 Oct A) is a fresh location made for this run: nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked there, so on the Dashboard the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices.
  • Labor rate {Rate-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100) charges $100.00 an hour at {Location-A}.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST C88632 Void Reinvoice) has one contact and one asset (for example unit ZZ-101).
  • {User-A} has Time Clock on and is the technician on the work.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S490-1201) for {Customer-A} is invoiced, not sent and not paid, and its Service Advisor is {User-A}.
  • {Work-order-1} has one labor line, {Line-1} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Line 1"), with technician {User-A}, labor rate {Rate-A}, Estimated Time 2.00 and Tech Time 2.00, and exactly 2.00 hours clocked on it.
  • You have written down the invoice's Subtotal (for example $200.00).
  • You run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record stays inside This Week.
  • You can open the release notes page on Confluence (https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=931069964).
custom_steps:
1. Click Reports in the top menu, then Sales in the left menu.
  2. Set the Date control to This week.
  3. Write down the row for {Work-order-1}'s invoice and the Subtotal in the Totals row.
  4. Click Advisor Analysis in the left menu (the page is titled Service Advisor Analysis) and set the Date control to This week, with no advisor chosen.
  5. Write down the invoice's row: Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Billing Efficiency, ELR and Subtotal.
  6. Click Work Orders in the top menu and open {Work-order-1}.
  7. On the Lines tab click New Line and add a second line: What Are You Doing? (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Line 2"), Add Technician {User-A}, Labor Rate {Rate-A}, Estimated Time 1.00, Tech Time 1.00, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close.
  8. On the new line click Story, type a short story and click Update.
  9. Click Complete on the new line (if a window offers Complete All Lines or asks for Mileage, finish it there), then click Mark Reviewed.
  10. Click the Finance tab and write down how it shows the first invoice.
  11. Click Create Invoice, close the New Customer Payment window without paying, and write down the new Subtotal.
  12. Open Reports > Sales again (Date: This week) and write down the rows and the Totals row Subtotal.
  13. Open Reports > Advisor Analysis again (Date: This week, no advisor chosen) and write down the rows and the Totals row.
  14. Click Parts > Part Sales > New Part Sale and try to invoice the sale without choosing a customer. If the screen insists on a customer, stop this step.
  15. Open the release notes page and find the Dashboard note that starts "Sales report totals can change".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 3 and 5: Before the void, the Sales report lists the invoice and its Totals row Subtotal is the amount you wrote down (for example $200.00). Advisor Analysis shows Hrs Worked 2.00, Hrs Invoiced 2.00 and Billing Efficiency 100.00% (2.00 / 2.00 x 100).
  • Steps 10 and 11: Write down how the Finance tab marks the first invoice (for example a Void label) and the new Subtotal (for example $300.00 = $200.00 + 1.00 hour x $100.00). These two readings are records, not pass or fail points.
  • Step 12: The Sales report lists only the new invoice: the voided invoice is gone, and the Totals row Subtotal equals the new Subtotal (for example $300.00), not the two added together (for example $500.00 = $200.00 + $300.00).
  • Step 13: Advisor Analysis shows one row for {Work-order-1}, the new invoice, with Hrs Invoiced 3.00 (2.00 + 1.00) and the new Subtotal (for example $300.00). Hrs Worked stays 2.00, so Billing Efficiency reads 150.00% (3.00 / 2.00 x 100). The figures moved up: this is the void-then-reinvoice case.
  • Step 14: If you could invoice a sale with no customer, it appears in the Sales report total and in Advisor Analysis. If the screen insisted on a customer, write "no-customer invoice not reachable by hand" in the result comment.
  • Step 15: The note says Sales report totals can change for some past dates: voided invoices are no longer counted, which lowers a total; invoices with no customer attached are now included, which raises one; and a voided invoice that was invoiced again counts only the new amount. It also says the Service Advisor Analysis report changes the same way and walk-in sales now count toward advisor figures. This checks the published notes, not the product screens.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas and Report Parity); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850, version 48 (14 Oct 2026, 17:09 UTC, Chris Ward), S3-E2 and its context notes (unchanged since version 42); read 14 Oct 2026. Release notes, Confluence 931069964 (version 7) and 928121200 (version 6), Dashboard "Worth knowing" note, changed on 14 Oct 2026 (15:07 UTC) by Chris Ward in answer to our question 2 of 14 Oct 2026; read 14 Oct 2026. Dashboard v1 Technical Implementation Plan (16 Sep 2026), NFR-010; it informs and never overrules the PRD. The note first published on 9 Oct 2026 said totals "can drop"; the note as changed on 14 Oct 2026 says they "can change", and we take the later note as prevailing. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.”
  • S3-E2 context note (Sales report): “That is a defect in the Sales report rather than a dashboard decision, and it is corrected inside this project so Revenue can match it (@chris ruling, 2026-09-15). Correcting it moves the Sales report's own existing totals for any range containing voided or no-company invoices, so it ships with a release note.”
  • S3-E2 context note (Service Advisor Analysis): “Service Advisor Analysis is a direct copy of the Sales report's invoice query and carries both flaws, so it is corrected in this project too (@chris ruling, 2026-09-16: the figures need to match each other and to be right, and today they are neither). That moves advisor revenue and ELR down for periods containing voided invoices and adds walk-in sales to advisor figures, under the same release note.”
  • Tech plan NFR-010: “Both report corrections ship with one plain-language release note: Sales report totals move for ranges containing voided or no-company invoices, and on Service Advisor Analysis revenue, ELR *and the hours columns, and therefore Labor Efficiency %* move for those periods, while advisor figures gain walk-in sales. It must also call out the void-then-reinvoice case, where a figure can move *up*”
  • Release notes, Dashboard, Worth knowing (Confluence 931069964 v7 and 928121200 v6, 14 Oct 2026): “Sales report totals can change for some past dates. Voided invoices are no longer counted, which lowers a total, and invoices with no customer attached are now included, which raises one. A voided invoice that was invoiced again counts only the new amount. The Service Advisor Analysis report changes the same way, and walk-in sales now count toward advisor figures. Expect questions about this.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
